To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DBN-pretrained systems can outperform GMM/HMM systems on datasets of 5870 hours and 1400+ hours.
the DBN-pretrained hybrid system outperforms a GMM/HMM system by 3.8% and 5.2% absolute WER on the two datasets.
DBN-pretrained ANNs can be used to build hybrid systems that outperform state-of-the-art GMM/HMM systems on large vocabulary ASR tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) The application of deep neural networks to ASR, (2) The application of DBN-pretrained ANNS to ASR, and (3) The use of large amounts of speech data in the training of DBN-pre-trained ANNS.

a) the use of DBN pretrained ANN/HMM systems for ASR b) the use of MMI and SCARF to further improve the performance and c) the use of a large vocabulary, low resource dataset to train the DBN pretrained ANN-HMM system.
the application of DBN-pretrained ANNHMM hybrid speech recognition systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

DBN-pretrained ANNHMM systems can outperform GMM/HMM systems by 3.9% absolute WER on a 5870 hour Voice Search task and by 5.6% absolute on a 1400 hour YouTube task, when the two systems are trained on similar amounts of data.
the DBN-pretrained system is the state-of-the-art on the two datasets.
DBN-pretrained hybrid systems have the potential to be competitive with GMM/HMM systems, but they require a large amount of data and careful tuning of the system to reach this potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DBN-pretrained system outperforms a GMM/HMM system trained with 10 times more data.
the DBN-pretrained system outperforms GMM/HMM systems on the first dataset by 3% absolute and 4.5% relative and on the second by 3.5% absolute and 6.5% relative.
the DBN-pretrained system outperforms all the baseline systems on the two datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
with large datasets, the pretrained ANN-HMM systems can outperform GMM-HMM systems.
the use of deep learning for pretraining of ANN/HMM systems for ASR is a viable approach even when the training data is very large.

DBN-pretrained ANNs can achieve state-of-the-art performance on ASR when trained on very large datasets, and can even achieve a lower error than GMM/HMM when trained on datasets that are an order of magnitude smaller.
